record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one find a simple, usable approximation scheme that accurately determines the gravitational radiation from an isolated astrophysical system, and in particular can one prove the quadrupole radiation formula?

evidence.quote: Find a simple, usable approximation scheme which allows one to determine (accurately) the gravitational radiation produced by an isolated astrophysical system. In particular, prove the quadrupole radiation formula.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an isolated self-gravitating astrophysical system modeled by an asymptotically flat solution of the Einstein field equations
$$R_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac12 R\, g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\, T_{\mu\nu},$$
where $g_{\mu\nu}$ is a Lorentzian metric on a 4-manifold, $R_{\mu\nu}$ and $R$ are its Ricci and scalar curvatures, and $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the stress-energy tensor of the matter content (for example, a perfect fluid or a finite collection of compact bodies). For such a system, define the (trace-free) mass quadrupole moment
$$Q_{ij}(t) = \int \rho(t,x)\Big(x_i x_j - \tfrac13 \delta_{ij}\, |x|^2\Big)\, d^3x$$
in a suitable Newtonian/post-Newtonian approximation, and let $h_{ij}^{TT}$ denote the transverse-traceless part of the metric perturbation in the far (radiation) zone of the system.

Problem. Construct a mathematically rigorous, simple, and practically usable approximation scheme that determines the gravitational radiation emitted by such an isolated system directly from the Einstein equations, and use it to give a rigorous derivation of the quadrupole radiation formula
$$h_{ij}^{TT}(t,r,\Omega) \;\sim\; \frac{2G}{c^4\, r}\, \ddot Q_{ij}^{TT}\!\left(t - \tfrac{r}{c}\right) \quad \text{as } r\to\infty,$$
with the corresponding energy flux
$$\frac{dE}{dt} \;=\; \frac{G}{5c^5}\, \langle \dddot Q_{ij}\, \dddot Q^{ij}\rangle,$$
establishing that this formula correctly describes the leading-order radiation of a bounded, slowly moving, weakly self-gravitating source as a controlled limit of full solutions of the Einstein equations.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial rigorous progress exists: Damour and Schäfer, Blanchet, and others derived the quadrupole formula within post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions, and Walker–Will and others established it as an asymptotic approximation in the Newtonian limit via the characteristic initial value formulation. However, a fully rigorous, broadly applicable derivation directly from the Einstein equations for general isolated astrophysical systems (including strong-field/compact binary regimes) is still regarded as incomplete, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational radiation and the validity of the far-zone quadrupole formula in the Newtonian limit of general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: The radiation carries an energy flux given asymptotically by the usual far-zone quadrupole formula, proving the quadrupole formula is an asymptotic approximation to general relativity.
status_evidence.claim: The quadrupole formula has been rigorously established as an asymptotic approximation in the Newtonian limit.

status_evidence.title: The quadrupole radiation formula
status_evidence.snippet: A rigorous version of the quadrupole radiation formula is derived using the characteristic initial value formulation of a general relativistic fluid space-time.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous derivations in restricted settings are available.

status_evidence.title: Quadrupole formula - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Einstein's 1918 result remains the leading-order 'quadrupole formula' for gravitational wave emission; rigorous justification has been studied via post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions.
status_evidence.claim: The formula is widely used and partially justified; complete rigorous derivation for general systems remains an active area.
